full_judgment:
2. Opposite party herein as plaintiff instituted Family Suit No. 53 of 2006 before the court of Assistant Judge, Boraigram, Natore impleading the petitioner herein as defendant praying for dower money and maintenance for herself and her 2 child contending inter alia that she got married with Md. Abu Musa @ Ibne Musa Mollah of same village on 27-3-2001 and subsequently marriage was dissolved by way of Khula Talak and thereafter they got married again on 5-10-2003 at dower money of Taka 39,999 and during the wedlock two male child were born, one during subsistence of first marriage and second one after re-marriage. The defendant drove away her on 18-6-2004 and since then she has been residing with her mother's house. The defendant did not give any maintenance to the plaintiff and children and also did not pay the dower money and, as such, she has been constrained to file the instant suit. 

 3. The present petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement Contending inter alia that the marital tie between the plaintiff and defendant was ceased by Khula Talak on 29-7-2003 and before that he paid the dower money amounting to Taka 8,000 to the plaintiff and consequently she relinquished her claim of maintenance and rest of the dower money. No marriage took place between the plaintiff and defendant for second time on 5-10-2003. During subsistence of marriage one male child was born between their wedlock and the claim of the plaintiff of having a second child is not in their wedlock. As the defendant paid dower money and the plaintiff relinquished her claim of maintenance, the suit as framed is not maintainable. 

 4. After hearing, the trial court decreed the suit in part so far the maintenance of child Bahauddin since 29-7-2003 until he goes to defendant's custody, but the trial court dismissed plaintiff's claim of second son holding that the plaintiff failed to substantiate the claim of second, marriage held on 5-10- 2003.The trial court also held that there exists no registered instrument of marriage between the plaintiff and defendant and the witnesses of the defendants clearly stated that no subsequent marriage took place between the plaintiff and defendant. The trial court disbelieved the evidence of the Witnesses of plaintiff. The appellate court decreed the suit as a whole in favour of the plaintiff contending that the witnesses of the plaintiffs proved the subsequent marriage between the plaintiff and defendant. The appellate court extracted the evidence of the witnesses of the plaintiff and found that all the plaintiff's witnesses supported plaintiffs claim and the appellate court also held that the witnesses of the defendants failed to substantiate the claim of the defendants that the plaintiff was married with Akter Hossain after divorce with the defendant. The appellate court also held that the second son namely Mehedi Hasan Rabbani is in fact was born during the wedlock between the plaintiff and defendant. From the side of the plaintiff-opposite party, Annexure-1 and 2 are filed to this court to prove the date of birth of the two children of the plaintiff and defendant. 

 5. Mr. Md. Zahedul Hoque, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the plaintiff failed to prove remarriage with the defendant as there was no kabinnama regarding the marriage between the plaintiff and defendant. He further submits that the evidence of the defendants witnesses is cogent, reasonable and sustainable but the appellate court reversed the findings of the trial court and decreed the suit as a whole. 

 6. Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan and Mr. SM Rezaul Karim, the learned Counsels appearing for the opposite party submits that the appellate court on consideration of facts and circumstances rightly decreed the suit entirely in favour of the plaintiffs. They further submit that the trial court without appreciating the evidence of the parties erroneously relied upon the evidence of the DWs and declined to grant decree for the plaintiff's maintenance and those of second child. They further submits that the trial court without any cogent reason disbelieved re marriage held between the plaintiff and defendant after Khula divorce. 

 7. Having heard the learned Counsel and on perusal of the materials on record it appears that the trial court disbelieved the plaintiffs claim of marriage with the defendant for 2nd time on the ground that there was no registered marriage deed between the parties and witnesses of the defendants stated that the plaintiff was married with one Akter Hossain for second time on 28-5-2008 while the trial court disbelieved the evidence of the plaintiffs witnesses, but on perusal of the witnesses of the plaintiff it appears that Harun-ar-Rashid deposed as PW 2 who stated that he is the Imam of Baratpur Moddhopara Jamea Mosjid and Moulana Abdus Samad Administered the marriage and he was present when marriage was administered. PW 3 Ful Chand who is also resident of village Baratpur stated that he was also present while marriage was administered by Moulvi Samad and the plaintiff and defendant have been living as husband and wife and two sons were born between the wedlock. PW 4 Abdus Samad stated that he administered marriage between the plaintiff and defendant on 5-10-2003 with dower money of Taka 39,999 and since then the plaintiff and defendant have been living as husband and wife. Now, turning to the evidence of DW 2 Ahmed Ali, who stated that marriage between plaintiff and Akter Hossain took place on 28-4-2008 while he was Imam of Dhulat village Mosque, but he stated that there was no registered marriage deed between the plaintiff and Akter Hossain. DW 3 Md. Kabil Uddin stated that he hails from village Dhulat and he came to know the plaintiff when she was taken to his home by his brother in law Nurshed who he stated that plaintiff will merry Akter Hossain, He further stated that the plaintiff came with two boys and two sons of her sister and he administered the marriage. DW 4 Abu Bakkar Siddique stated that in the wedlock of plaintiff and defendant one son was born and Khola Talak was held between them, but he does not know how much amount has been paid to the plaintiff at the time of Talak. He stated that he was not aware whether the plaintiff married again married the defendant after Khula Talak. From the evidence of DW 3 Md. Kabil Uddin it appears that plaintiff came to his house with two boys along with two boys of her sister when the marriage took place between plaintiff and Akter Uddin. From the evidence of DW 3 also it is clear that when the plaintiff came to his house she has two sons. So, the contention of second son having born between the wedlock of plaintiff and Akter Hassain is not correct. Apart from this the witnesses of the defendant also knew Harun-ar-Rashid as Imam of Baratpur Jamea Mosjid and Ful Chand and Moulvi Abdus Samad, so, considering the evidence of the plaintiffs and defendant in juxtaposition, claim of the plaintiff is consistent and reliable. The finding of the appellate court in respect of marriage for second time and a child having born between the wedlock more reasonable and sustainable. 

 10. It appears that the trial court granted maintenance for the plaintiff as well as son @ Taka 500 which is not unreasonable given the facts and circumstance and social condition of the parties. As the plaintiff came to her parents house on 18-6-2004 she and her first child is entitled to get maintenance from that date onward. So far the second child is concern, Mehedi Hasan Rabbani was born at her maternal grandparents house and, as such, he is entitled to get maintenance from that date onward until he attains 18 years and the plaintiff is also entitled to get maintenance until the marriage between the plaintiff and defendant is terminated by lawful means.
